typed_core.name: document_title
typed_core.why: identity — the only reliable signal of what a Custom doc actually is

typed_core.name: document_subtype
typed_core.why: disambiguator — which family this instance belongs to (asset / credit / disclosure), collapsed from the catalog's three parallel *_subtype fields

typed_core.name: party_name
typed_core.why: identity — primary named party (flattened from party_names / owner/borrower blocks)

typed_core.name: party_count
typed_core.why: disambiguator — how many parties the raw string held

typed_core.name: property_address
typed_core.why: identity — links to subject/non-subject property when present

typed_core.name: loan_number
typed_core.why: identity — links to the loan file

typed_core.name: primary_amount
typed_core.why: processor — the headline money value when the doc has one (market value / balance / fee)

nested_lists.name: unmapped_key_value_pairs
nested_lists.shape_reason: a Custom document's real content is unknown at schema-design time, so the only safe structure is a generic key/value passthrough. Flat rows keep it light. This is the single nested list. Item count is unbounded

fields.name: label
fields.why: the verbatim label of an unmapped fact on the document

fields.name: value
fields.why: the verbatim value paired with the label
fields.pii_note: any PII the model reads on a Custom document will land here unmasked; the list needs the transaction-description redactor pattern or a per-value PII sweep before it is trusted

rejected.reason: family-specific; only meaningful once the doc is classified — belong to the real doc type, not Custom

current_or_market_value, cash_or_liquid_value, net_available_value, ownership_percentage, encumbrance_or_loan_balance, valuation_date
disclosure_title, creditor_broker_or_provider, disclosed_terms, disclosure_date, opt_in_or_opt_out_status, acknowledgment_or_consent_text
supporting_line_items, fees_or_amounts, consumer_choices_or_elections, deductions_or_offsets, event_or_delinquency_dates

encoding_variations: Because 'Custom' spans many document families, the same fact (a date, an amount, a party) is encoded differently every time. document_subtype is the disambiguator that tells the rest of the pipeline how to interpret the generic fields.

open_questions.q: Should 'Custom' have a schema at all? It is a fallback for unclassified documents.
options: no dedicated schema — route to a pure catch-all extractor
open_questions.recommendation: (a), because even a generic identity header lets a processor attach the document to a borrower/loan GEET'S DECISION (LP-439): yes — a thin identity schema lets a processor attach the document to a borrower/loan.

open_questions.q: unmapped_key_value_pairs and PII. A key/value passthrough can capture SSNs, account numbers, addresses unmasked.
options: require a redactor sweep over this list before it is persisted
open_questions.recommendation: require a redactor sweep over this list before it is persisted, or cap it to non-sensitive labels. Must be resolved before Custom is trusted GEET'S DECISION (LP-439): declare a redact over unmapped_key_value_pairs' value (LP-437's _DESC_REDACT) — the explicit safety gate; Custom is not trusted until the redactor is declared.

open_questions.q: primary_amount ambiguity. Collapsing market value / balance / fee into one field loses meaning.
options: drop if reviewers find it misleading
open_questions.recommendation: keep it only as a rough headline and rely on document_subtype; drop if reviewers find it misleading

open_questions.q: document_subtype collapse. The catalog offers three distinct subtype fields.
open_questions.recommendation: confirm a single collapsed field is acceptable, or whether classification upstream already resolves family

notes: No rules today, and this is not a real document type — it is a catch-all bucket whose catalog stacks three unrelated family blocks (asset, credit, disclosure) plus the shared identity header. A single typed-core schema cannot faithfully serve an arbitrary document. The design is deliberately thin and under the ~20-field target: a small identity core that always applies, one subtype disambiguator, and a key/value passthrough.

No PII field is promoted here because the content is unknown. Risk: any PII the model reads on a Custom document will land in unmapped_key_value_pairs or the catch-all unmasked. The key/value list needs the transaction-description redactor pattern, or a per-value PII sweep, before it is trusted for arbitrary documents.

Prompt hint (doc-level): tell the model this is an unclassified / vendor-specific document — extract the identity header faithfully, put everything else into unmapped_key_value_pairs with verbatim labels, and never invent structure. Do not force values into asset/credit/disclosure shapes; if the document is not that family, those fields are null.
